Samir: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selector tweak p99 latency on long sequences in rtx-pool jumped.
Lia: Which workloads? sequence length distribution? :thinking_face:
Samir: Chatgen workloads, median seq ~80 but 5% > 1024. p50 unchanged, p95 +10ms, p99 +70ms. Tail events correlate with KV misses and a kernel fallback to generic matmul.
Devin: Do we have kernel selection logs? could be that small_attn_v2 is being skipped for some shapes.
Samir: Pasted excerpt of selector log:
```
[2026-03-14T09:12:33Z] model=v2-serialized batch_tokens=512 seq=128 kernel_chosen=small_attn_v2 fallback=matmul reason=kv_stall
[2026-03-14T09:12:34Z] batcher:max_batch_tokens=4096 max_wait_ms=8
kv_hit_rate=0.78 tail_kv_miss=0.22 kv_load_ms_p99=95ms
```
Lia: kv_load_ms_p99 95ms — that's huge. Where is the stall coming from? serialization/unpacking? disk-backed KV page faults?
Anya: Rolling GC observed around same time on one node, and we saw ephemeral FS I/O spikes. Could be eviction thrash on the local cache shards.
Devin: Two levers to try: 1) reduce max_wait_ms to lower queueing tail (better p99 at cost of batching/throughput), 2) reduce max_batch_tokens so small_attn_v2 path stays valid and avoids fallback.
Samir: I ran a synthetic sweep on a canary: lowering max_wait_ms 8->3 reduced p99 by ~40ms but qps dropped 8%. Reducing max_batch_tokens 4096->2048 kept qps similar but avoided fallback in many cases; p99 improved ~30ms.
Lia: Interesting. Any change to KV hit rate after adjustments?
Samir: yes — with smaller batches KV hit_rate improved to 0.86 (less cross-request interleaving causing extra KV fetches), tail_kv_miss down to 0.12.
Devin: Suggest we also try a token-threshold-based kernel guard: if per-request tokens > 512 force small_attn_v2 path even for odd batch shapes — essentially prefer attention kernel over generic matmul for those sequences.
Anya: That would be a kernel preference heuristic. Implementation risk: might increase memory or contention; need perf test.
Samir: Proposed experiment plan:
1) A/B: baseline vs (max_wait_ms=3, max_batch_tokens=2048)
2) Separate A/B: baseline vs kernel-pref-threshold (per_req_token_threshold=512)
3) Monitor p50/p95/p99, qps, kv_hit_rate, kv_load_ms_p99
Config snippet for canary:
```
{
  "batcher": {"max_batch_tokens": 2048, "max_wait_ms": 3},
  "kernel": {"per_req_token_threshold": 512, "prefer_kernel": "small_attn_v2"}
}
```

Anya: I'll run the sweep today during low traffic window and collect traces + kernel-selection logs. Will also attach flamegraphs for KV hot paths.
Lia: Make sure to capture tail traces (p99 traces) and include kernel fallback counts. Add a break-down per seq-length bucket.
Devin: If kernel-pref reduces throughput too much we can add adaptive fallback: prefer small_attn_v2 but revert if observed latency per batch > threshold.
Samir: OK assigning: Anya runs runs and posts results; Devin will prototype the kernel-pref heuristic; Lia will set up dashboards for per-length p99 and kv metrics.
Anya: noted. I'll post back with initial numbers and a short summary.
Samir: Thanks — goal is to get p99 under SLA without >10% qps regression. :thumbsup:
